issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, and the exercise text instructs implementing it as an int-returning method, but the provided solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object (and includes a StudentCount class). The template does not provide a StudentCount type and students are expected to implement a method that returns an int per the UML. This mismatch between the specified return type (int) and the solution's return type (StudentCount) will confuse students and prevent them from matching the intended API and tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement and template by changing getTotalNumberOfStudents() in Lecture to return an int (the sum of inscribed and guest students) instead of a StudentCount object, and update any callers (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to use the int value. Alternatively, if introducing StudentCount is intentional, update the UML and problem text to specify StudentCount as the return type and add StudentCount to the template so students can compile and follow the design. Prefer the first option to preserve the current UML and exercise intent.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task text) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning an int, but the solution represents the same conceptual entity (the total number of students) with a new class named StudentCount and implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount instance. This introduces a different identifier (StudentCount) for the same concept described in the problem, creating a mapping barrier: students reading the task expect a primitive int result while the solution uses a wrapper type with a getValue() method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the total number of students consistent with the problem statement. Either (A) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return a primitive int (sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove or avoid using StudentCount, updating dependent methods accordingly; or (B) update the problem statement/UML to document and justify the StudentCount wrapper type (and mention its name) so students can map the requirement to that identifier. Prefer option A to match the original UML return type and reduce student confusion.
